newsitem.title: USA: Chase credit card losses stabilizing - CFO.
newsitem.headline: Chase credit card losses stabilizing - CFO.

text.p: Credit card loss levels at Chase Manhattan Corp have begun to level off due to the company's efforts to slow the rate of growth at the business, Chase's chief financial officer said.

While the bank continues to forecast long-term double-digit earnings per share growth, with some $2.5 billion now budgeted for share buybacks through 1998, chief financial officer Peter Tobin said Chase's payout ratio might slip from the 30 percent in earnings it is currently paying.

"Earlier this year we said we would consider a 25 to 35 percent level, meaning while we were increasing our dividend we would certainly think about stock buybacks at the same time," Tobin said on a conference call.
"I think it is possible our dividend payout could drop a little bit but on the whole we would still expect to see increases in dividend levels," he said.
Regarding credit card charge-off levels, Tobin said, "We really feel as though the numbers have stabilized."
Tobin said slower credit card portfolio growth, achieved through additional credit screens, has helped control losses.
As a result, delinquencies "have actually been trending down for the last two or three quarters," he said, and bankruptcies, while high, have begun to stabilize.

Credit card net charge-offs, which ran at 4.95 percent of average managed receivables in the third quarter, "might be up a few basis points" next quarter, he said, but the bank was sticking with a forecast of "just under 5.0 percent for the full year."
